record.paper_title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let A be a sectorial operator on an L^p-space with p in (1, infinity), and assume that -A generates a contractive C_0-semigroup. Must A then have a bounded H-infinity calculus, have bounded imaginary powers, or be R-analytic?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Let A be a sectorial operator on some Lp-space for p ∈ (1, ∞) and suppose that −A is the generator of a contractive C0-semigroup. Does A have a bounded H∞-calculus (bounded imaginary powers / is R-analytic)?
Definition 2.7 (Bounded H∞-calculus). A sectorial operator A is said to have a bounded H∞(Σσ)-calculus for some σ ∈ (ω(A), π) if the homomorphism f 7→ f(A) from H∞0 (Σσ) to B(X) is bounded.

Definition 2.12 (Bounded Imaginary Powers (BIP)). A sectorial operator on a Banach space X is said to have bounded imaginary powers (BIP) if for all t ∈ R the operator Ait associated to the functions λ 7→ λit via the holomorphic functional calculus is bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and let $A$ be a sectorial operator on an $L^p$-space $L^p(\Omega,\mu)$. Recall that a closed densely defined operator $A$ on a Banach space $X$ is called sectorial of angle $\omega\in[0,\pi)$ if its spectrum is contained in the closed sector $\overline{\Sigma_\omega}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}:|\arg z|\le\omega\}\cup\{0\}$ and for every $\sigma\in(\omega,\pi)$ one has $\sup\{\|\lambda(\lambda-A)^{-1}\|:\lambda\notin\overline{\Sigma_\sigma}\}<\infty$; the infimum of such $\omega$ is the sectoriality angle $\omega(A)$.

For $\sigma\in(0,\pi)$ let $H^\infty(\Sigma_\sigma)$ denote the algebra of bounded holomorphic functions on the open sector $\Sigma_\sigma$, and $H^\infty_0(\Sigma_\sigma)$ its subalgebra of functions $f$ satisfying $|f(z)|\le C\min(|z|^s,|z|^{-s})$ for some $s,C>0$. For a sectorial $A$ with $\omega(A)<\sigma$, the holomorphic functional calculus defines $f(A)\in B(X)$ for $f\in H^\infty_0(\Sigma_\sigma)$ via a Cauchy integral. One says that $A$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus if $\|f(A)\|\le C\|f\|_\infty$ for all $f\in H^\infty_0(\Sigma_\sigma)$ for some $\sigma\in(\omega(A),\pi)$.

One says that $A$ has bounded imaginary powers (BIP) if for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$ the operator $A^{it}$ given by the holomorphic functional calculus extends to a bounded operator on $X$.

One says that $A$ is $R$-analytic if $A$ generates a bounded analytic semigroup $(e^{-zA})_{z\in\Sigma_\theta}$ for some $\theta>0$ such that the family $\{e^{-zA}:z\in\Sigma_{\theta'}\}$ is $R$-bounded for every $\theta'\in(0,\theta)$, where a family $\mathcal{T}\subset B(X)$ is $R$-bounded if there exists $C>0$ with
$$\Big\|\sum_{k=1}^n r_k T_k x_k\Big\|_{L^2([0,1];X)}\le C\Big\|\sum_{k=1}^n r_k x_k\Big\|_{L^2([0,1];X)}$$
for all $T_k\in\mathcal{T}$, $x_k\in X$ and Rademacher functions $r_k$.

Assume in addition that $-A$ generates a $C_0$-semigroup of contractions on $L^p(\Omega,\mu)$, i.e. $\|e^{-tA}\|_{B(L^p)}\le 1$ for all $t\ge 0$.

Question: Must $A$ have a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus? Must $A$ have bounded imaginary powers? Must $A$ be $R$-analytic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every negative generator of a contractive $C_0$-semigroup on an $L^p$-space ($p\in(1,\infty)$) has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus (or BIP, or $R$-analyticity) is a long-standing open problem in the functional-calculus theory of sectorial operators. On Hilbert space ($p=2$) it follows from a result of Le Merdy that contractive semigroups have $H^\infty$-calculus, but for general $p$ no proof or counterexample appears to be known, and recent surveys and lecture notes still list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Regularity Properties of Sectorial Operators: Counterexamples and Open Problems (zbMATH listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing this as an open problem on contractive semigroups on L^p.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an open problem in the literature on sectorial operators.

status_evidence.title: Semigroup theory via functional calculus (Haase)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses bounded H-infinity calculus of generators of contractive semigroups, with the L^p case open beyond the Hilbert space setting.
status_evidence.claim: The L^p case (p≠2) of contractive-semigroup generators having bounded H∞-calculus is not known.
